```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

Xu 2020 used a stepwise translational analysis to choose the doses of a human
PET study of JNJ-54175446, a brain-penetrant P2X7 receptor antagonist:

1. a human population PK/PD model of the single and multiple ascending dose
   studies, with the ex vivo stimulated IL-1beta release as the PD readout;
2. an exposure-occupancy model fitted to monkey PET data and translated to
   human by correcting the EC50 for plasma protein binding;
3. simulation of human brain occupancy with the population PK model and the
   translated occupancy model, later compared with the human PET data, to
   which the same exposure-occupancy model was also fitted.

The paper contributes three models, all documented here:

| Model | Content |
|---|---|
| `Xu_2020_jnj54175446` | Human population PK (Table 1) and the IL-1beta release PD model (Eq. 2) |
| `Xu_2020_jnj54175446_ro` | Human brain receptor occupancy vs. average plasma concentration over the PET scan (Table 2, human) |
| `Xu_2020_jnj54175446_ro_monkey` | Rhesus monkey brain receptor occupancy vs. average plasma concentration over the PET scan (Table 2, monkey) |

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Xu_2020_jnj54175446"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1111/cts.12711> (open access, PMC7070800)

```{r models}
mod_pk <- readModelDb("Xu_2020_jnj54175446")
mod_ro <- readModelDb("Xu_2020_jnj54175446_ro")
mod_ro_monkey <- readModelDb("Xu_2020_jnj54175446_ro_monkey")
ui_pk <- rxode2::rxode(mod_pk)
ui_ro <- rxode2::rxode(mod_ro)
ui_ro_monkey <- rxode2::rxode(mod_ro_monkey)
```

# Population

The population PK/PD model was fitted to 2,560 plasma concentrations from 107
healthy adults in the phase 1 single ascending dose (SAD, NCT02475148) and
multiple ascending dose (MAD, NCT02515955) studies: median age 31 years (range
18-69), median weight 77.3 kg (46.5-113.4), 87% White and 97% men. All doses
were an oral liquid formulation: single 0.5-300 mg doses fasted, single 50, 300
and 600 mg doses after a high-fat breakfast, and 50-450 mg once daily for 10
days with a standard breakfast (Results; Table S1). Of the subjects, 39% were
fasted, 16% had a high-fat meal and 45% a standard meal.

The human occupancy model was fitted to 16 PET occupancy measures from 8
healthy men given two single oral doses each (5-300 mg with a standard
breakfast), with plasma sampled at about 4, 4.75 and 6 h after the dose. The
monkey occupancy model was fitted to 5 measures from two rhesus macaques (one
male, 12.1 kg; one female, 8.7 kg) given intravenous doses of 0.1-5.3 mg/kg 10
min before the tracer.

The same information is available programmatically via the `population`
metadata of each model, e.g. `readModelDb("Xu_2020_jnj54175446")()$population`.

# Source trace

Each `ini()` value carries an in-file comment naming its source. Table numbers
refer to Xu 2020; File S1 is the paper's example NONMEM code.

| Model | Parameter / equation | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| PK/PD | `lka` | log(0.428) 1/h | Table 1 'K a' |
| PK/PD | `lcl` | log(5.10) L/h | Table 1 'CL/F' (70 kg) |
| PK/PD | `lvc` | log(272) L | Table 1 'V/F' (70 kg) |
| PK/PD | `e_wt_cl`, `e_wt_vc` | 0.426, 1.14 | Table 1 'BWT on CL/F', 'BWT on V/F'; footnotes c, e |
| PK/PD | `logitffo` | logit(1 - 0.0760) | Table 1 'FK0'; Results '92.4%' first-order |
| PK/PD | `ld2` | log(1.05) h | Table 1 'TK0'; File S1 `D2=TK0` |
| PK/PD | `ltlag`, `ltlag2` | log(0.287), log(2.03) h | Table 1 'ALAG1', 'ALAG2' |
| PK/PD | `e_dose_fdepot` | 0.178 | Table 1 'beta'; Eq. 1 |
| PK/PD | `e_fed_fdepot`, `e_fed_highfat_fdepot` | 1.63, 1.76 | Table 1 'E FOOD' rows; Results '76% and 63% higher' |
| PK/PD | `etalka`, `etalcl`, `etalvc` | 1.04^2, 0.300^2, 0.198^2 | Table 1 IIV rows (CV% = sqrt(omega^2) x 100) |
| PK/PD | `propSd` | 0.175 | Table 1 'Proportional residual error' |
| PK/PD | `e0`, `etae0` | 798 pg/mL, 206^2 | Table 1 'E 0', 'IIV of E 0' (normal IIV, Methods) |
| PK/PD | `limax` | log(747) pg/mL | Table 1 'Emax' |
| PK/PD | `lic50`, `etalic50` | log(67.0) ng/mL, 0.449^2 | Table 1 'EC50,IL1beta' (0.0670 ug/mL), IIV row |
| PK/PD | `lhill` | log(4.9) | Not tabulated; digitised from Figure 5 (see below) |
| PK/PD | `addSd_il1b` | 199 pg/mL | Table 1 'Additive residual error' |
| PK/PD | Absorption: depot (F1, ALAG1) + central zero-order (F2, ALAG2, D2) | -- | Figure 2; File S1 `$PK` |
| PK/PD | `Fr = exp(-beta * DOSE / 150) * EFOOD` | -- | Eq. 1; File S1 `F1`, `F2` |
| PK/PD | `Cc = 1000 * central / vc` (ng/mL) | -- | File S1 `S2 = V/1000` |
| PK/PD | `il1b = E0 - Imax * Cc^gamma / (IC50^gamma + Cc^gamma)` | -- | Eq. 2 |
| RO, human | `lemax`, `lec50`, `lhill` | log(78.3) %, log(44.3) ng/mL, log(1.43) | Table 2, human |
| RO, monkey | `lemax`, `lec50`, `lhill` | log(56.0) %, log(43.2) ng/mL, log(3.71) | Table 2, monkey |
| RO | `ro = Emax * CAV^gamma / (EC50^gamma + CAV^gamma)` | -- | Eq. 3 |
| Translation | EC50 human = EC50 monkey x fu,monkey / fu,human = 43.2 x 17.0 / 11.2 | 65.6 ng/mL | Eq. 4; Results |

# Event-table helper

Every oral administration is two dose records: the first-order arm into
`depot`, and the zero-order arm into `central` with `rate = -2` so that the
modelled duration `dur(central)` is used. `f()` and `alag()` in the model
apply each arm's fraction and lag, so both records carry the full dose amount
at the nominal dosing time. The dose level enters relative bioavailability
through the `DOSE_JNJ54175446_MG` column.

```{r helpers}
meal_cols <- function(meal) {
  data.frame(
    FED = as.integer(meal %in% c("standard", "high-fat")),
    FED_HIGHFAT = as.integer(meal == "high-fat")
  )
}

# Weight: log-normal around the cohort median 77.3 kg, truncated to the
# observed 46.5-113.4 kg range (Results).
draw_wt <- function(n) {
  wt <- exp(rnorm(3 * n, log(77.3), 0.15))
  wt <- wt[wt >= 46.5 & wt <= 113.4]
  wt[seq_len(n)]
}

make_cohort <- function(n, dose, meal, n_doses = 1, obs_times, treatment,
                        id_offset = 0L, wt = draw_wt(n)) {
  ids <- id_offset + seq_len(n)
  dose_times <- (seq_len(n_doses) - 1) * 24
  doses <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = dose_times, cmt = c("depot", "central")) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      amt = dose, evid = 1L,
      rate = ifelse(cmt == "central", -2, 0),
      dvid = NA_integer_
    )
  obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = obs_times) |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, rate = 0, cmt = NA_character_, dvid = 1L)
  dplyr::bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    dplyr::left_join(data.frame(id = ids, WT = wt), by = "id") |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      DOSE_JNJ54175446_MG = dose,
      meal_cols(meal)[rep(1, dplyr::n()), ],
      treatment = treatment
    ) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}
```

Observation rows carry `dvid = 1` and no `cmt`: the model has two endpoints
(`Cc` and `il1b`), and a forward solve returns every model variable as a
column on those rows.

# Structural checks (typical values)

```{r structural}
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(ui_pk)

# Typical-value solves of several subjects at once: rxode2 warns that a
# multi-subject simulation has no omega, which is the intent here. Only that
# message is muffled.
solve_typical <- function(events, ...) {
  withCallingHandlers(
    rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events, returnType = "data.frame", ...),
    warning = function(w) {
      if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w))) invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
    }
  )
}

grid_sd <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 12, by = 0.05), seq(12, 2000, by = 1))))
cases <- data.frame(
  dose = c(0.5, 50, 150, 600, 50, 300),
  meal = c("fasted", "fasted", "fasted", "fasted", "high-fat", "standard")
)
ev_typ <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(cases)), function(i) {
  make_cohort(1, cases$dose[i], cases$meal[i], obs_times = grid_sd,
              treatment = paste(cases$dose[i], "mg", cases$meal[i]),
              id_offset = i - 1L, wt = 70)
}))
sim_typ <- solve_typical(ev_typ, keep = "treatment", rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12)
stopifnot(!anyNA(sim_typ$Cc))

# Closed form: AUC0-inf = Fr * dose / (CL/F) * 1000 (ng*h/mL); 2000 h is
# about 54 half-lives, so the truncation is negligible.
food <- c(fasted = 1, standard = 1.63, `high-fat` = 1.76)
cases$fr <- exp(-0.178 * cases$dose / 150) * food[cases$meal]
cases$auc_closed <- cases$fr * cases$dose / 5.10 * 1000
cases$auc_sim <- sapply(seq_len(nrow(cases)), function(i) {
  x <- sim_typ[sim_typ$id == i, ]
  sum(diff(x$time) * (head(x$Cc, -1) + tail(x$Cc, -1)) / 2)
})
cases$rel_err <- cases$auc_sim / cases$auc_closed - 1
knitr::kable(cases, digits = c(1, 0, 3, 0, 0, 5),
             caption = "Typical-value AUC0-inf (70 kg) against the closed form Fr x dose / (CL/F).")
# The trapezoid on a 0.05-h / 1-h grid carries ~1e-4 discretisation error;
# a wrong Fr factor, unit or dose record moves this by tens of percent.
stopifnot(max(abs(cases$rel_err)) < 2e-3)

# Zero-order arm: a closed-form one-compartment solution of both arms for
# 150 mg fasted. The zero-order input runs from ALAG2 = 2.03 h to
# 2.03 + 1.05 = 3.08 h.
fr <- exp(-0.178)
ka <- 0.428; kel <- 5.10 / 272
first_order <- function(t) {
  tt <- pmax(t - 0.287, 0)
  fr * 0.924 * 150 * ka / (ka - kel) * (exp(-kel * tt) - exp(-ka * tt))
}
zero_order <- function(t) {
  r0 <- fr * 0.076 * 150 / 1.05
  infused <- pmax(pmin(t, 3.08) - 2.03, 0)
  r0 / kel * (1 - exp(-kel * infused)) * exp(-kel * pmax(t - 3.08, 0))
}
chk <- sim_typ[sim_typ$id == 3 & sim_typ$time <= 12, ]
closed <- 1000 * (first_order(chk$time) + zero_order(chk$time)) / 272
stopifnot(max(abs(chk$Cc - closed)) < 1e-4 * max(closed))
```

The packaged model reproduces the closed-form AUC for every dose and meal
condition, and the full 0-12 h profile of the parallel zero-order /
first-order absorption, including the delayed zero-order arm.

# Population PK: visual predictive check (Figure 3)

Figure 3 of Xu 2020 shows the VPC by study and dose. The SAD panels at 50 and
300 mg pool a fasted and a high-fat arm; they are simulated fasted here, and
600 mg (given only with a high-fat meal) with a high-fat meal. The MAD arms
received once-daily doses for 10 days with a standard breakfast.

```{r vpc_sim}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20200309)
set.seed(20200309)
n_arm <- 100
t_sad <- c(0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 24, 36, 48, 72, 96, 120, 144)
t_mad <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 24, by = 1), seq(24, 216, by = 24),
                       216 + c(1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 24, 36, 48, 72, 96, 120, 144))))
arms <- tibble::tribble(
  ~study, ~dose, ~meal, ~n_doses,
  "SAD", 0.5, "fasted", 1,
  "SAD", 2.5, "fasted", 1,
  "SAD", 10, "fasted", 1,
  "SAD", 50, "fasted", 1,
  "SAD", 150, "fasted", 1,
  "SAD", 300, "fasted", 1,
  "SAD", 600, "high-fat", 1,
  "MAD", 50, "standard", 10,
  "MAD", 100, "standard", 10,
  "MAD", 150, "standard", 10,
  "MAD", 300, "standard", 10,
  "MAD", 450, "standard", 10
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = factor(paste(study, dose, "mg"), levels = paste(study, dose, "mg")))

ev_vpc <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(arms)), function(i) {
  make_cohort(n_arm, arms$dose[i], arms$meal[i], n_doses = arms$n_doses[i],
              obs_times = if (arms$study[i] == "SAD") t_sad else t_mad,
              treatment = as.character(arms$treatment[i]),
              id_offset = (i - 1L) * n_arm)
}))
sim_vpc <- rxode2::rxSolve(ui_pk, ev_vpc, keep = "treatment", returnType = "data.frame")
stopifnot(!anyNA(sim_vpc$Cc))
sim_vpc$treatment <- factor(sim_vpc$treatment, levels = levels(arms$treatment))
```

```{r vpc_plot, fig.height = 8, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 3 of Xu 2020: simulated median (line) and 5th-95th percentiles (band) of JNJ-54175446 plasma concentration, including residual error, by study and dose (100 virtual subjects per arm)."}
vpc <- sim_vpc |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    p05 = quantile(sim, 0.05), p50 = median(sim), p95 = quantile(sim, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
ggplot(vpc, aes(time, p50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), fill = "grey80") +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~treatment, scales = "free", ncol = 3) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "JNJ-54175446 (ng/mL)") +
  theme_bw()
```

The simulated medians follow the published VPC panels: a peak of about
350 ng/mL after 150 mg fasted (published model median about 300 ng/mL),
about 550 ng/mL after 300 mg, and day-9 to day-10 levels of roughly
1300-1800 ng/mL at 150 mg and 2600-3600 ng/mL at 450 mg once daily. The one
arm that sits visibly high is 600 mg with a high-fat meal: the simulated
median peak is about 1400 ng/mL, against about 1000-1100 ng/mL in the
published panel. That arm combines the strongest dose effect on Fr
(exp(-0.178 x 4) = 0.49) with the high-fat factor, and no parameter was
adjusted to close the gap.

```{r vpc_assert}
# Medians read from the published VPC panels (Figure 3) with generous bands:
# a transcription error in CL/F, V/F, Fr or the dose effect moves these by
# far more than the band.
med_at <- function(trt, t) vpc$p50[vpc$treatment == trt & vpc$time == t]
stopifnot(
  med_at("SAD 150 mg", 6) > 200, med_at("SAD 150 mg", 6) < 450,
  med_at("MAD 150 mg", 216) > 1000, med_at("MAD 150 mg", 216) < 2500,
  med_at("MAD 450 mg", 216) > 2000, med_at("MAD 450 mg", 216) < 5000
)
```

# PKNCA: single-dose NCA

```{r pknca}
sad <- sim_vpc |>
  dplyr::filter(grepl("^SAD", treatment), !is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment) |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = as.character(treatment))
sad <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  sad,
  sad |> dplyr::distinct(id, treatment) |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, treatment, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, treatment, time)
dose_sad <- ev_vpc |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1, cmt == "depot", grepl("^SAD", treatment)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, treatment)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sad, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_sad, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
                        aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
nca_sum <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment, PPTESTCD) |>
  dplyr::summarise(median = median(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median) |>
  dplyr::arrange(as.numeric(sub("SAD ([0-9.]+) mg", "\\1", treatment)))
nca_sum |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, cmax, tmax, aucinf.obs, half.life) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Arm" = treatment, "Cmax (ng/mL)" = cmax, "Tmax (h)" = tmax,
    "AUC0-inf (ng*h/mL)" = aucinf.obs, "t1/2 (h)" = half.life
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Median simulated single-dose NCA by SAD arm (100 subjects per arm).")
```

Xu 2020 does not tabulate NCA results; its Introduction summarises the SAD
study as a median Tmax of 2-4 h under fasted conditions and an elimination
half-life of about 35 h. The comparison below uses the 150 mg fasted arm.

```{r nca_compare}
published <- tibble::tibble(treatment = "SAD 150 mg", tmax = 3, half.life = 35)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res |> (\(x) {
    x$result <- x$result[x$result$treatment == "SAD 150 mg", ]
    x
  })(),
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(tmax = "h", half.life = "h"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated vs. reported (Xu 2020 Introduction) NCA, 150 mg fasted. * differs from the reference by >20%.")

hl <- nca_sum$half.life[nca_sum$treatment == "SAD 150 mg"]
# Expected median: log(2) * V/F / CL/F at the 77.3 kg cohort median weight,
# 0.693 * 272 * 1.104^1.14 / (5.10 * 1.104^0.426) = 39.7 h, i.e. about 13%
# above the rounded '~35 h'. Median-of-100 Monte-Carlo SE is about 2 h
# (CV of t1/2 ~36%), so the 35% band sits more than 3 SE from 39.7 h, while
# a CL/F or V/F transcription error of 2-fold or more fails it.
stopifnot(abs(hl / 35 - 1) < 0.35)
```

The median half-life (about 40 h at the cohort's median weight of 77.3 kg;
37 h at 70 kg) agrees with the reported ~35 h. The simulated median Tmax is
later than the 2-4 h reported for the fasted SAD arms. This is a property of
the published model rather than of the implementation (the typical-value
profile above matches its closed form): the population typical ka of 0.428 1/h
places the typical Tmax near 8 h, and Xu 2020 itself notes that the fit was
less good in the absorption phase. No parameter was adjusted.

# Food and dose effects on exposure

```{r food}
auc_of <- function(d, m) cases$auc_sim[cases$dose == d & cases$meal == m]
ratio_hf <- auc_of(50, "high-fat") / auc_of(50, "fasted")
ratio_hf
stopifnot(abs(ratio_hf - 1.76) < 0.01)
```

With the high-fat meal the AUC rises by 76% at the same dose, in the range
of the 50-70% (50 mg) and 50-111% (300 mg) increases observed in the SAD food
cohorts (Discussion). Exposure is less than dose-proportional:
`r round(cases$auc_sim[cases$dose == 600] / cases$auc_sim[cases$dose == 0.5] / 1200, 2)`
is the ratio of dose-normalised AUC at 600 mg to that at 0.5 mg, equal to
exp(-0.178 x (600 - 0.5) / 150).

# Ex vivo IL-1beta release (Figure 5, red)

```{r il1b_curve, fig.cap = "Replicates the IL-1beta curve of Xu 2020 Figure 5: typical ex vivo stimulated IL-1beta release against plasma concentration."}
conc_grid <- 10^seq(0, 4, length.out = 200)
il1b_typ <- 798 - 747 * conc_grid^4.9 / (67^4.9 + conc_grid^4.9)
ggplot(data.frame(conc = conc_grid, il1b = il1b_typ), aes(conc, il1b)) +
  geom_line(colour = "firebrick") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-500, 2500)) +
  labs(x = "Concentration (ng/mL)", y = "IL-1beta (pg/mL)") +
  theme_bw()
```

The IL-1beta model is evaluated inside the packaged model; the check below
reads `il1b` from the typical-value solve and compares it with the Eq. 2
expression at the solved concentration.

```{r il1b_check}
x <- sim_typ[sim_typ$id == 3, ]
il1b_eq2 <- 798 - 747 * x$Cc^4.9 / (67^4.9 + x$Cc^4.9)
stopifnot(max(abs(x$il1b - il1b_eq2)) < 1e-6)

# MAD: 'approximately full and continuous antagonism of IL-1beta stimulation
# at doses >= 50 mg/day' (Introduction). Typical value at the day-10 trough
# (216 h, i.e. 24 h after the ninth dose) of 50 mg once daily.
ev_mad50 <- make_cohort(1, 50, "standard", n_doses = 10, obs_times = c(24, 216),
                        treatment = "MAD 50 mg", wt = 70)
mad50 <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev_mad50, returnType = "data.frame")
knitr::kable(mad50[, c("time", "Cc", "il1b")], digits = 1,
             caption = "Typical trough concentration and IL-1beta release, 50 mg once daily.")
stopifnot(all(mad50$il1b < 798 - 0.9 * 747))
```

Already 24 h after the first 50 mg dose the typical trough concentration is
well above the IL-1beta IC50 of 67 ng/mL, so the release is inhibited by more
than 90% throughout the dosing interval.

# Brain receptor occupancy

## Monkey model (Figure 4a)

```{r ro_monkey, fig.cap = "Replicates Xu 2020 Figure 4a: monkey brain P2X7 receptor occupancy vs. average plasma concentration over the PET scan."}
cav_grid <- 10^seq(0, 3.5, length.out = 200)
# The occupancy models are algebraic in CAV and carry no IIV, so each input
# value is one row of a single subject (a multi-subject solve of a model
# without omega warns).
ro_ev <- function(cav) {
  data.frame(id = 1L, time = seq_along(cav) - 1, evid = 0L, amt = 0, CAV = cav)
}
ro_mk <- rxode2::rxSolve(ui_ro_monkey, ro_ev(cav_grid), returnType = "data.frame")
ggplot(data.frame(cav = cav_grid, ro = ro_mk$ro), aes(cav, ro)) +
  geom_line(colour = "blue") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 80)) +
  labs(x = "Average concentration (ng/mL)", y = "Receptor occupancy (%)") +
  theme_bw()
stopifnot(abs(rxode2::rxSolve(ui_ro_monkey, ro_ev(43.2), returnType = "data.frame")$ro - 28) < 1e-6)
```

## Translation to human and dose selection (Figure 4b, Table S3)

Eq. 4 scales the monkey EC50 by the ratio of plasma fractions unbound,
43.2 x 17.0 / 11.2 = `r round(43.2 * 17.0 / 11.2, 1)` ng/mL, keeping Emax and
gamma. Xu 2020 then simulated occupancy 4-6 h after single doses with a
standard meal, with EC50 at 0.2 to 5 times this value. Here the average
concentration over 4-6 h is taken from the typical-value PK model and passed
to the monkey model with its EC50 overridden.

```{r table_s3}
doses_s3 <- c(5, 10, 12.5, 25, 50, 100, 150, 200, 300, 450, 600)
ev_s3 <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(doses_s3), function(i) {
  make_cohort(1, doses_s3[i], "standard", obs_times = seq(4, 6, by = 0.05),
              treatment = paste(doses_s3[i], "mg"), id_offset = i - 1L, wt = 70)
}))
pk_s3 <- solve_typical(ev_s3)
cav_s3 <- pk_s3 |>
  dplyr::group_by(id) |>
  dplyr::summarise(cav = sum(diff(time) * (head(Cc, -1) + tail(Cc, -1)) / 2) / 2)
ec50_h <- 43.2 * 17.0 / 11.2
mult <- c(0.2, 0.5, 1, 2, 5)
s3_sim <- sapply(mult, function(m) {
  rxode2::rxSolve(ui_ro_monkey, ro_ev(cav_s3$cav),
                  params = c(lec50 = log(m * ec50_h)), returnType = "data.frame")$ro
})
s3_pub <- matrix(c(
  49.3, 11.0, 1.02, 0.0800, 0.00266,
  55.4, 42.6, 11.0, 1.03, 0.0347,
  55.7, 49.2, 20.0, 2.30, 0.0794,
  56.0, 55.4, 49.2, 20.1, 1.02,
  56.0, 56.0, 55.4, 49.3, 11.0,
  56.0, 56.0, 56.0, 55.4, 42.6,
  56.0, 56.0, 56.0, 55.9, 52.3,
  56.0, 56.0, 56.0, 56.0, 54.7,
  56.0, 56.0, 56.0, 56.0, 55.7,
  56.0, 56.0, 56.0, 56.0, 55.9,
  56.0, 56.0, 56.0, 56.0, 56.0
), ncol = 5, byrow = TRUE)
s3_tab <- data.frame(dose = doses_s3, cav = cav_s3$cav)
for (j in seq_along(mult)) {
  s3_tab[[paste0(mult[j], "x sim")]] <- s3_sim[, j]
  s3_tab[[paste0(mult[j], "x pub")]] <- s3_pub[, j]
}
knitr::kable(s3_tab, digits = 1,
             caption = "Simulated (typical value) vs. published (Table S3) human brain occupancy (%) by dose and EC50 multiple; cav is the 4-6 h average concentration (ng/mL).")
# Absolute occupancy difference, percentage points; the curve is steep
# (gamma 3.71), so a few-percent concentration difference moves the
# mid-range entries by a few points.
stopifnot(max(abs(s3_sim - s3_pub)) < 6, median(abs(s3_sim - s3_pub)) < 0.5)
```

```{r fig4b, fig.cap = "Replicates Xu 2020 Figure 4b: simulated human brain occupancy 4-6 h after single doses with a standard meal, EC50 at 0.2 to 5 times the value translated from monkey."}
s3_long <- data.frame(dose = rep(doses_s3, length(mult)),
                      ro = as.vector(s3_sim),
                      ec50 = factor(rep(paste0(mult, "x EC50"), each = length(doses_s3)),
                                    levels = paste0(mult, "x EC50")))
ggplot(s3_long, aes(dose, ro, colour = ec50)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(x = "Dose (mg)", y = "Receptor occupancy (%)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

All five EC50 values give near-maximal occupancy at 150 mg, the basis on which
Xu 2020 chose 150 mg as the first PET dose. The simulated occupancies agree
with Table S3 to within a few percentage points; the differences sit on the
steep part of each curve.

The concentrations behind Table S3 can be recovered by inverting the Emax
function. They are exactly proportional to dose, about 4.48 ng/mL per mg from
5 to 150 mg, whereas the packaged model's Fr declines with dose as Eq. 1
specifies (the 4-6 h average falls from 4.9 to 4.1 ng/mL per mg over the same
range). The Table S3 simulation therefore did not apply the dose effect on Fr;
its constant scale matches Fr = 1.76 x exp(-0.178), i.e. the Eq. 1 value at
150 mg with the factor 1.76. The packaged model follows Eq. 1 and the File S1
code.

```{r table_s3_implied}
implied <- function(ro, ec50) ec50 * (ro / (56 - ro))^(1 / 3.71)
per_mg <- c(
  implied(1.02, ec50_h) / 5, implied(1.03, 2 * ec50_h) / 10,
  implied(20.0, ec50_h) / 12.5, implied(20.1, 2 * ec50_h) / 25,
  implied(11.0, 5 * ec50_h) / 50, implied(42.6, 5 * ec50_h) / 100,
  implied(52.3, 5 * ec50_h) / 150
)
round(per_mg, 2)
stopifnot(diff(range(per_mg)) < 0.05)
```

## Human PET data (Figure 4c, 4d)

```{r fig4cd, fig.cap = "Replicates Xu 2020 Figures 4c and 4d: human brain occupancy vs. average concentration over the PET scan, predicted from monkey (EC50 65.6 ng/mL, Emax 56%, gamma 3.71) and fitted to the human PET data (Table 2)."}
ro_h <- rxode2::rxSolve(ui_ro, ro_ev(cav_grid), returnType = "data.frame")
ro_tr <- rxode2::rxSolve(ui_ro_monkey, ro_ev(cav_grid),
                         params = c(lec50 = log(ec50_h)), returnType = "data.frame")
dplyr::bind_rows(
  data.frame(cav = cav_grid, ro = ro_tr$ro, model = "Translated from monkey (Fig. 4c)"),
  data.frame(cav = cav_grid, ro = ro_h$ro, model = "Fitted to human PET (Fig. 4d)")
) |>
  ggplot(aes(cav, ro, colour = model)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_x_log10() +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 100)) +
  labs(x = "Average concentration (ng/mL)", y = "Receptor occupancy (%)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
stopifnot(
  abs(rxode2::rxSolve(ui_ro, ro_ev(44.3), returnType = "data.frame")$ro - 78.3 / 2) < 1e-6
)
```

## Occupancy in the PET study design

Combining the population PK model with the human occupancy model reproduces
the integrated PK/occupancy analysis for the PET study doses (single doses with
a standard breakfast, plasma averaged over the 4-6 h scan).

```{r pet_design, fig.cap = "Simulated human brain occupancy (median and 90% interval, 100 virtual subjects per dose) for the PET-study doses, from the population PK model and the human occupancy model."}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20191109)
set.seed(20191109)
pet_doses <- c(5, 10, 20, 50, 150, 300)
ev_pet <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(pet_doses), function(i) {
  make_cohort(100, pet_doses[i], "standard", obs_times = seq(4, 6, by = 0.25),
              treatment = paste(pet_doses[i], "mg"), id_offset = (i - 1L) * 100L)
}))
pk_pet <- rxode2::rxSolve(ui_pk, ev_pet, keep = c("treatment", "DOSE_JNJ54175446_MG"),
                          returnType = "data.frame")
cav_pet <- pk_pet |>
  dplyr::group_by(id, DOSE_JNJ54175446_MG) |>
  dplyr::summarise(cav = sum(diff(time) * (head(Cc, -1) + tail(Cc, -1)) / 2) / 2,
                   .groups = "drop")
cav_pet$ro <- rxode2::rxSolve(ui_ro, ro_ev(cav_pet$cav), returnType = "data.frame")$ro
pet_sum <- cav_pet |>
  dplyr::group_by(dose = DOSE_JNJ54175446_MG) |>
  dplyr::summarise(cav_median = median(cav), ro_p05 = quantile(ro, 0.05),
                   ro_median = median(ro), ro_p95 = quantile(ro, 0.95))
knitr::kable(pet_sum, digits = 1)
ggplot(pet_sum, aes(dose, ro_median)) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = ro_p05, ymax = ro_p95)) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(x = "Dose (mg)", y = "Receptor occupancy (%)") +
  theme_bw()
stopifnot(
  pet_sum$ro_median[pet_sum$dose == 150] > 0.9 * 78.3,
  pet_sum$ro_median[pet_sum$dose == 5] < 0.5 * 78.3
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **IL-1beta Hill coefficient digitised.** Eq. 2 has a sigmoidicity factor
  gamma, but Table 1 reports none, and a simple Emax model (gamma = 1) cannot
  produce the Figure 5 curve, which falls from E0 to E0 - Emax between about
  40 and 110 ng/mL. The maintainers digitised seven points on the falling limb
  of the Figure 5 model curve and fitted the logit of the fractional inhibition
  against log concentration: gamma = 4.94, with the midpoint at 67.5 ng/mL,
  which reproduces the tabulated EC50 of 67.0 ng/mL. The model uses
  gamma = 4.9.
- **No IIV on the IL-1beta Emax.** The Methods say IIV was assumed for Emax
  and EC50, but Table 1 reports IIV only for E0 and EC50; the final model is
  taken to have none on Emax.
- **IIV on E0 read as an SD.** Table 1 gives 206 for the normally distributed
  E0 IIV without a CV, which is read as an SD in pg/mL (variance 206^2); a
  variance of 206 pg^2/mL^2 would be negligible next to the 199 pg/mL residual
  error.
- **Fr at the reference dose.** The text says Fr = 1 at 150 mg fasted, but
  Eq. 1 and the File S1 code give Fr = exp(-0.178 x DOSE / 150), which is 0.837
  at 150 mg. The model follows the equation and the code, so CL/F and V/F are
  apparent values relative to Fr = 1 at zero dose; the half-life is unaffected.
  Table 1 lists beta in 1/h, but it multiplies a dimensionless dose ratio and is
  itself dimensionless.
- **Meal coding.** The Methods and File S1 code FOOD = 1 as a high-fat and
  FOOD = 2 as a standard meal, while the Table 1 rows label the codes the
  other way round. The Methods, the Table 1 descriptions and the Results
  ('76% and 63% higher', for high-fat and standard meals respectively) all
  pair 1.76 with the high-fat meal and 1.63 with the standard meal, which is
  what the model encodes through `FED` and `FED_HIGHFAT`. Taken literally,
  the Table 1 code labels together with the File S1 coding would give the
  opposite pairing; the Table S3 scale (below) is also consistent with 1.76
  for a standard meal, and the 600 mg high-fat VPC arm runs high. Neither is
  decisive against three explicit statements, so the stated pairing is kept;
  swapping the two factors changes exposure by 8%.
- **Table S3 used dose-proportional exposure.** See the section above: the
  published occupancies imply 4.48 ng/mL per mg at every dose, so that
  simulation did not apply the dose effect on Fr. The packaged model is not
  altered to match it. The Results text also gives the EC50 range as
  '13-325 ug/mL'; the values are ng/mL (Table S3: 13.1-328 ng/mL).
- **Residual error.** File S1 shows a combined proportional and additive error
  model, but Table 1 reports only a proportional term (17.5%); the model is
  proportional only.
- **Receptor-occupancy models are typical-value only.** Table 2 reports no IIV
  and no residual error for either occupancy model, so `ro` is a derived
  output with no error model. The occupancy models take the average plasma
  concentration over the PET scan (`CAV`) as input, as in the paper; for
  simulation, compute it from `Xu_2020_jnj54175446` over the scan window
  (4-6 h after an oral dose in human).
- **SAD arms of Figure 3.** The 50 and 300 mg SAD panels pool fasted and
  high-fat subjects; the VPC here simulates them fasted.
- **Virtual cohort.** Weight was drawn log-normal around the 77.3 kg median,
  truncated to 46.5-113.4 kg. The PET cohort's demographics are not reported,
  so the same distribution was used.
- **Errata.** No correction notice for Xu 2020 was found (Europe PMC search,
  2026-11-27).
